description: Strategy POS: prove ordinary two-point cancellation (contradiction from a persistent correlation)

outcome: abandoned (own conflict + all children failed); revisited as I.a4
obstruction: A dilation graph joins n and n+hd only when d | n, a sparse condition. Removing (centering) that condition costs either reciprocal mass (comparable-size primes, I.a1.1) or scale (wide dilations, I.a1.2). Tao's entropy decrement avoids the dilemma only at an unspecified scale (I.a1.3).
lesson: The central difficulty is removing sparse divisibility conditions without changing the scale (C3a). Any graph must have both large reciprocal mass and scale localization.
generality: general (it states the problem's core trade-off for every graph approach)
known_in_literature: Known: this is the ordinary-vs-logarithmic averaging gap. Log averages are dilation invariant (Tao 2016, Forum Math Pi), ordinary averages are not. Helfgott-Radziwill 2021 and Pilatte 2023/26 work on…
influence: decisive: I.a4 meets both requirements, with weights A^{omega(d)} for mass and narrow multiplicative intervals for scale
salvage: The graph framework itself is kept and resumed at I.a4 (L65).

description: Graph steps with primes of comparable size
obstruction: Primes in one dyadic-type range [P, 2P] have reciprocal mass sum 1/p ~ 1/log P, which is far too small to drive graph expansion or a spectral saving.
lesson: One range of comparable primes has too little reciprocal mass, so the mass must be amplified, by many ranges or weighted products (C2).
known_in_literature: Known: the reciprocal-mass budget is the basic constraint in Helfgott-Radziwill (arXiv:2103.06853). Pilatte's composite labels (products of primes from several ranges) exist to amplify it.
influence: decisive: weights A^{omega(d)} giving the broad degree (1+A)^{omega_S(n)} (I.a4.1). Part II analogue: J supplies of mass ~W each, total W^J (II.b1.7; cross-part reuse inferred).

description: Graph steps with broader dilations (wide prime ranges)
obstruction: Dilations n -> dn by d of very different sizes compare averages at different scales X and X/d. An ordinary average at the terminal scale cannot absorb that comparison; a logarithmic average can.
lesson: Steps must be localized to a narrow multiplicative window, so all dilations in one comparison have essentially the same size (C3).
generality: general (rules out naive transfers of log-averaged graph arguments to ordinary averages)
known_in_literature: Known: this is the reason Tao 2016 and HR/Pilatte are logarithmic. The paper's intro says logarithmic weighting 'combines information from many multiplicative scales'.
influence: decisive: narrow intervals near a scale H (I.a4.3, I.a4.5); paper's 'short multiplicative intervals' (H<d<=tau H) in both parts

description: Tao's entropy-decrement argument [13]
obstruction: Entropy decrement finds SOME scale where the independence estimate holds (pigeonhole over scales). It cannot be forced to hold at the given terminal scale, so it yields log-averaged or almost-all-scales results only.
lesson: Entropy-decrement methods choose an unspecified scale and cannot give every-scale ordinary cancellation (C4).
generality: general (rules out the Tao/Tao-Teravainen family as a direct route)
known_in_literature: Known: Tao 2016 (log averages), Tao-Teravainen 2019 (exceptional scales of log density 0), KMT 2023 (full upper log density).
influence: contributory: relearned at I.a4.9; the final fixed-B-then-X->infinity order of limits (I.a4.18) controls one prescribed scale B, which is the opposite design (inferred)

obstruction: Ergodicity gives a dilation-invariant formulation, but the invariant measure is infinite, so the simple invariant-probability argument fails. Normality of the limiting state remains an extra assumption.
lesson: Ergodicity with infinite measure plus an unproved normality assumption does not give cancellation (C7).

lesson: Sign-preserving polynomial substitutions have sparse images; a positive-density argument is still needed (C10).

Consider the Goemans-Williamson near-satisfiable Max-Cut guarantee [29] and Raz's odd-cycle obstruction to strong parallel repetition [52] (as an attempted route to near-1 completeness from Max-Cut-type gaps).

Problem (Part I): for every prime p, field K of char p, group G and a,b in K[G], does ab=1 imply ba=1? Proof or certified counterexample.
Strategy PROVE-1: prove direct finiteness in positive characteristic (substitute for the char-0 trace positivity; or reduce char 2 to char 0).
obstruction: Every positivity substitute (Witt lifts, entropy, pivot densities, skew coefficients, spectral atoms, valuations, determinants, sign lifting) needs a conservation/positivity/uniqueness principle that the model cannot prove for arbitrary (nonamenable, nonsofic) groups.
lesson: Positive-characteristic direct finiteness has no available positivity mechanism; every route either assumes an approximation property (sofic/surjunctive) or reduces to an open conjecture (Luck determinant).
known_in_literature: Known state of the art: positive results only for sofic (Elek-Szabo 2004), residually amenable / free-by-amenable (Ara-O'Meara-Perera 2002), surjunctive groups (Phung 2023; CSCP 2025).
influence: enabling: the first switch to constructing a counterexample follows the accumulation of these failures.
salvage: ULIE reduction (a4), DJ finite-factor reduction (a9), defect idempotent q=1-ba framing (a1).

description: Orientation: known sufficient hypotheses (surjunctivity [12,13], sofic [19]); organize the search by the defect idempotent q=1-ba (q^2=q, aq=qb=0).
Witt-vector lifting to obtain a zero-trace idempotent.
obstruction: A Witt-vector lift of the defect idempotent q suggests a zero-trace idempotent, but nothing forces a zero-trace idempotent to vanish without positivity (char-0 faithful trace) or an analytic continuation.
lesson: Lifting coefficients does not import positivity; a zero trace is not a contradiction without a faithful positive trace (K2).
known_in_literature: Known: in char p the Kaplansky trace of an idempotent lies in the prime field (Zalesskii 1972) and carries no positivity; Montgomery 1969 / Kaplansky need a positive faithful trace.
influence: contributory (start of the positivity clause K2)

description: Entropy approach: strict entropy decrease on proper linear subshifts (CA/Garden-of-Eden style).
obstruction: Entropy strictly decreasing on proper linear subshifts is a Garden-of-Eden (Moore-Myhill) argument valid for amenable groups; on nonamenable groups naive (Folner) entropy is unavailable.
lesson: Entropy/dimension counting needs amenability or soficity; it cannot cover arbitrary groups (K3).
known_in_literature: Known: Garden-of-Eden theorem for amenable groups (Ceccherini-Silberstein-Machi-Scarabotti 1999); failure for nonamenable groups; sofic entropy needs soficity.

description: Universal left-invertible-element (ULIE) groups of Dykema-Heister-Juschenko [17]: reduce to finite cancellation patterns.
Random-priority pivot densities as an algebraic dimension; conservation argument.
obstruction: A dimension defined by densities of pivots under random priority orders needs a conservation identity obtained by differentiating infinite-volume quantities; phase transitions may make these non-differentiable.
lesson: Finite-volume conservation identities do not pass to infinite volume across phase transitions (K4).
known_in_literature: Known phenomenon (non-uniqueness of Gibbs measures; cf. Lyons-Peres on nonamenable percolation).
salvage: the random-priority device is reused in a13 and a33.4

description: Enlarge coefficients to a skew group ring.
obstruction: Passing to a skew group ring with larger coefficients only reformulates direct finiteness as an equally open rank condition.
lesson: Coefficient enlargement relocates, not removes, the difficulty (K5).
known_in_literature: Known in spirit (crossed products of DF rings need not be DF; Ara-O'Meara-Perera use rank functions).

description: Spectral amplification: forbidden rational spectral atom from repeated defect summands; Thom [37,38], Balci-Skandalis [4].
obstruction: Amplifying the defect produces rational spectral atoms, but excluding them needs a determinant lower bound known only for sofic groups (Thom; determinant conjecture).
lesson: Spectral/determinant routes are conditional on the determinant conjecture or a sofic hypothesis (K6).
known_in_literature: Known: Elek-Szabo 2005 (determinant conjecture for sofic groups); Thom 2008; Dodziuk-Linnell-Mathai-Schick-Yates 2003.
influence: contributory; cross-family: inverted in the companion Determinant-Conjecture counterexample, whose input is this family's char-2 pair
salvage: spectral reduction reused in a30, a33

description: Char-2 sign lifting: replace cancelling pairs x_i y_j = x_k y_l by x_i y_j = z x_k y_l with a central involution z, so a char-2 cancellation becomes a char-0 one (contradicting Kaplansky in char 0).
Reduced row cycles give reduced column words (encouraging); odd-area spherical diagrams defeat the parity justification that z survives.
obstruction: The twisted presentation must keep z nontrivial; spherical van Kampen diagrams of odd area force z=1, and the pairing of equal products is forced when equality classes have size 2.
lesson: Sign lifting needs a central involution that survives; odd-area spherical diagrams can kill it, and with classes of size exactly two there is no alternative pairing (K7).
lesson_form: negative result (counterexample to the parity argument)
generality: general for sign-lifting from char 2 to char 0
known_in_literature: Related to Gardam's units (char 2 and C) [20,21]; the specific obstruction appears new as stated.
influence: enabling: becomes the explanation why the final char-2 construction cannot lift (D=0 in K)

description: Recall Gardam's nontrivial units in char 2 and over C [20,21] as a model for lifting.
obstruction: Gardam's char-2 units and his later complex units are found by different searches; they supply no general principle lifting char-2 identities to char 0.
lesson: No general lifting principle from char-2 units to char-0 units is available.
known_in_literature: Known (Gardam 2021 and arXiv:2312.05240 use separate constructions).

description: Reformulate the row graph as an immersion into a graph with column-labelled edges.

lesson: No stated lesson.

description: Survey of reductions: finite coefficient fields, surjunctivity; Dykema-Juschenko: stable finiteness of K[G] <=> direct finiteness of K[G x H] for all finite H [18]; continued ULIE encoding [17].
Random valuations as a substitute for positive Hilbert-space geometry (distinct leading weights).
obstruction: Valuations prevent finite cancellation but give no convergence for infinite elimination, and coercivity does not imply surjectivity.
lesson: Valuations are not a positivity substitute (instance of K2).
known_in_literature: Known: leading-term arguments prove zero-divisor results for orderable groups only.

description: Amplify a hypothetical defect through lamp projections and tensor powers: integral positive operators with negative log-determinant, conditional on Luck's determinant conjecture; Manzoor IRS [28].
obstruction: The amplification produces an integral positive operator with negative log-determinant, contradicting the determinant conjecture; but that conjecture is unproved for the relevant (arbitrary) groups, and Manzoor's IRS result does not remove the hypothesis.
lesson: A DF counterexample would contradict the determinant conjecture; the route is conditional (K6).
known_in_literature: Known direction: DF and determinant/approximation conjectures are linked through soficity (Elek-Szabo 2004, 2005); Manzoor arXiv:2508.15154.
influence: cross-family: this reduction, read contrapositively, is the content of the companion Determinant-Conjecture counterexample (same family)
salvage: the reduction reappears in a30, a33 and as the spectral atom -1/2 in e1.4.20

description: Narrower lemma: collisions under conjugation occur at isolated indices or periodically; an idempotent e with (1-e)te=0 for a group element t also satisfies (1-e)t^{-1}e=0.
outcome: partial (lemma kept; extension to sums open)
obstruction: The single-element lemma obstructs compression of an idempotent by one group element; extending to sums of group elements (the actual b) remained open.
lesson: Idempotents cannot be compressed by a single group element (K8); sums are the real difficulty.
known_in_literature: Not found in the literature as stated; related to Kaplansky's trace arguments.

description: Strategy CEX-1: construct a, b with ab=1, ba!=1 (finite-subgroup averages, designs, one-sided algebras, subgroup embeddings).
obstruction: Constructions either collapse the group (dense identifications), become directly finite by a rank argument (split relations), or violate the size bound (high girth).
lesson: A counterexample needs faithfully embedded finite subgroups, compatible character projections, and a reciprocal-size budget (K9, K11, K12).

obstruction: Designs produce the forward cancellation, but the presented groups collapse or violate curvature constraints, killing the reversed defect.
lesson: Group-theoretic realization (non-collapse) is the binding constraint for design-based cancellations (K9).
known_in_literature: Known phenomenon (dense small-cancellation presentations collapse; triangle groups of finite groups need curvature conditions, Gersten-Stallings 1991).

description: Polynomial matrices over the one-sided algebra k<x,y|xy=1> to lift forward Laurent identities while preserving a reversed defect.
Simplest construction.
obstruction: Constant-intersection restrictions block the simplest polynomial-matrix lift.
lesson: Simplest Jacobson-algebra lifts are blocked.
known_in_literature: The Jacobson algebra k<x,y|xy=1> is the universal non-DF algebra (Jacobson 1950); its non-embeddability in group algebras is the conjecture itself.

description: Split Leavitt families and singular matrices; closing word-count argument unfinished; then (sec 3 opening) a corrected rank argument handles the special split-relations construction.

known_in_literature: Leavitt algebras are not DF but do not embed in group algebras over fields of this type; folklore.
salvage: rank-counting as a detection tool (reappears as the augmentation rank certificate)

description: Odd-order finite subgroups whose nonidentity elements cancel with even multiplicity; averaging projectors give a rectangular factorization; need faithful subgroup embeddings and compatible character projections.
obstruction: Averaging idempotents e_K = |K|^{-1} sum_{g in K} g (odd |K| is invertible in char 2) produce a rectangular one-sided inverse if the subgroups embed faithfully, but dense identifications collapse and high-girth gluings cost too much size.
lesson: Subgroup averages are the right mechanism; the remaining problem is the girth-vs-size trade-off (K11).
known_in_literature: Averaging idempotents of finite subgroups are standard (Passman, The Algebraic Structure of Group Rings); their use to build one-sided inverses is new as far as known.
influence: decisive (necessary: the final criterion is exactly this mechanism)
salvage: averaging idempotents, rectangular factorization, character projections, girth requirement

known_in_literature: Known: Jung GAFA 2007; Hayes IMRN 2018.

description: Generator-dependent microstate entropy -> width dimension
obstruction: Microstate entropy has unknown W*-invariance; width dimension has no probabilistic lower bound (rounding); equivariance does not cut the parameter count.
lesson: Microstate-dimension invariants of the Minkowski or width type cannot be made generator-independent with available tools (C5a, C5, C6).
known_in_literature: Known open problem (Voiculescu invariance). The final paper proves non-invariance of delta, delta_0, delta*, delta^star.

description: Minkowski-type microstate entropy
obstruction: Microstate free entropy (dimension) is generator-dependent. W*-invariance is Voiculescu's open problem. Polynomial approximations of new generators in old ones are only L2-close ("bad approximations"), so microstate spaces cannot be transported.
lesson: Minkowski-type microstate dimension cannot be shown W*-invariant (C5a); switch to topological/mean/width dimension.
known_in_literature: Known open problem (Voiculescu, Free entropy survey 2002, sec 2.6, cited in the paper). The final paper proves the NON-invariance (Cor. cor:entropy-dimensions).
influence: decisive for the immediate sibling a5.2 (verbatim proposal of width/mean dimension)

description: Width dimension: upper bound nN^2 vs required lower bound ~sN^2
obstruction: Suppose s free semicirculars are recoverable from n<s generators. Polynomial approximation then gives a width upper bound nN^2 for NxN microstates, and a contradiction needs a lower bound ~sN^2 under stringent moment constraints. A commutative rounding example keeps approximate recovery while sharply reducing coarse dimension. Finite-quotient models lose too many parameters. High-probability (con…
lesson: The width lower bound cannot come from probability alone, because rounding cheats (C5).
lesson_form: negative result + sharpened target (the missing piece is exactly a uniform widt…
known_in_literature: Apparently new in this setting; it is analogous to the known gap between measure-theoretic and topological dimension (Gromov waist/width).
influence: decisive for sibling a5.3 (equivariance proposed to rule out rounding)

description: Exploit unitary equivariance of trace-polynomial approximants
obstruction: Trace-polynomial approximants are unitarily equivariant with N-independent degree, which rules out entrywise rounding. But tensor-twisted embeddings preserve free distributions while retaining infinitely many Fourier coefficients, so the parameter count still fails.
lesson: Equivariance does not restrict the effective parameter count (C6).
known_in_literature: apparently new (unverifiable)
influence: none visible (width ideas resurface at c3 L254-256, where the lesson is not cited)

description: Algebraic L2-homology (Connes-Shlyakhtenko) vs continuous vanishing (Popa-Vaes)
obstruction: Connes-Shlyakhtenko L2-Betti numbers of the group algebra C[F_n] give n-1, but they are defined for a dense *-subalgebra and their W*-invariance is open. Popa-Vaes (IMRN 2015) show that the continuous first L2-cohomology vanishes for every II1 factor, so the W*-continuous variant cannot distinguish.
lesson: Generator-independent (continuous) L2-cohomology is constant (zero), and the algebraic version is not known to be invariant (C7).
known_in_literature: Known barrier (Connes-Shlyakhtenko 2005 raise the invariance question; Popa-Vaes 2015; Thom 2008).
influence: contributory (reapplied at a7, a10, a17.1, a28, c1)

description: Adjoin nonseparable auxiliary factors; derivations on restricted domains
obstruction: Extensions by nonseparable auxiliary factors reduce to a separable support algebra; BDIP again cannot be transported. Popa-Vaes vanishing prompts derivations on restricted domains.
lesson: Nonseparable auxiliaries collapse to separable data (C1 again).
known_in_literature: Known (as a1).

description: Free-Jacobian rank via factoring polynomial approximations through fewer variables
obstruction: Factoring polynomial approximations through fewer variables bounds the free-Jacobian rank, but derivatives are not controlled in the limit. A commutative checkerboard example shows that strong convergence of bounded kernels need not preserve module rank, and gradient relations give no uniform estimate.
lesson: Jacobian/derivative ranks do not survive approximation without derivative control (C8).
lesson_form: negative result + constraint on future approaches
generality: general (any argument that differentiates approximate generator changes)
known_in_literature: Known in spirit: rank bounds for non-microstates free entropy dimension hold for polynomials or regular functions, not for W*-functions (Shlyakhtenko; Charlesworth-Shlyakhtenko 2016; Mai-Speicher-Web…
influence: DECISIVE for the final design: the final route avoids differentiating residuals (L283-284, "keep residuals small without differentiating them") and uses operator-norm estimates (L297-304). Relearned …

description: Boundary approach: proper proximality, free Hilbert transforms, Julg-Valette index
obstruction: Free groups are properly proximal; Mei-Ricard free Hilbert transforms give regularity; the Julg-Valette tree operator gives a Fredholm-type index for maps L2(M) -> L2(M)^r with weakly compact commutators. A shift on normalized vectors supported on shrinking orthogonal projections removes the index defect and preserves regularity: in a II1 factor, small projections absorb integer defects.
lesson: Index or K-theoretic defects are not W*-stable (C9).
generality: general (rules out index/K-theory-type invariants at the von Neumann level)
known_in_literature: Known folklore: K-theoretic distinctions of C*_r(F_n) (Pimsner-Voiculescu K1 = Z^n) do not pass to the II1 closure, where Breuer index is real-valued.
influence: contributory (pruning at a13 and a23; verification at d1.3.6). Its mirror image C21 (norm-continuous constructions ARE constrained by C*-invariants) is decisive for d1.3.
salvage: the Julg-Valette picture is re-recognised at L98 and L180; used positively as a consistency check at L327-329 (Weyl-von Neumann absorption)

description: Contradict absorption Q1*Q2 = Q1*Q2*L(F_inf) with rigid components; L2-homology again
obstruction: Under an affirmative answer, Dykema-Radulescu give Q1*Q2 = Q1*Q2*L(F_inf) for all II1 factors Q1, Q2. Ioana-Peterson-Popa rigidity tracks rigid components but not the added free part. Algebraic L2-homology meets derivations not determined by weakly dense generators.
lesson: Absorption with rigid components gives no contradiction; derivations are not determined on dense generators (C10).
known_in_literature: Known (Dykema-Radulescu 2003; IPP 2008; the domain problem is standard).

description: Ringrose automatic continuity; Shen generator invariant; Ge-Popa; Jung back-and-forth
obstruction: Ringrose's automatic continuity needs Banach-bimodule targets, not affiliated (unbounded) ones. Shen's generator invariant G(M) scales as t^{-2} under amplification (Dykema-Sinclair-Smith-White), but its positivity for free group factors is unknown. Ge-Popa blocks a finite-generation shortcut, and Jung's characterisation of amenability by embeddings into R^omega limits back-and-forth.
lesson: Generator-number invariants lack a positive lower bound (C11); automatic continuity fails for affiliated targets.
known_in_literature: Known (Shen 2009; DSSW 2008 explicitly state the positivity question; Jung 2007).

description: L(F_inf) copies near finite sets; Gaboriau cost / l2-Betti coupling
obstruction: The idea was to place copies of L(F_inf) near finite sets. Adjoining missing coordinates imposes conjugacy relations, and spectral gap obstructs perturbing them into free bases. Gaboriau cost and measure-equivalence invariance of l2-Betti numbers rely on measurable relabeling that is EXACT on large sets, whereas operator approximations are only L2-close.
lesson: Operator approximations give only L2-closeness, not exact agreement on large sets (C12).
lesson_form: negative result + sharpened target (the missing step is identified explicitly)
known_in_literature: Known (the absence of a cost invariant for II1 factors is a standard open theme; Shlyakhtenko on free entropy and cost).
salvage: The spectral-gap obstruction to perturbing into free bases foreshadows C19 (b1.4).

description: Self-similar corners; matrix-amplification distinguished row (Wick first-letter stripping)
obstruction: Dykema's compression formula suggests self-similar corners, but identifying a corner with the original factor requires generator collapse, which is circular. In the matrix-amplification row argument, stripping the first letter of a Wick expansion has bounded total L2 norm. But bulk errors on a projection of trace ~1/k give order-one row errors, and the row space L2(M) minus C is the Julg-Valette …
lesson: Shrinking corners consume recovery information and rescaling magnifies errors by 1/t (C13); the row argument is the Julg-Valette obstruction (C9).
known_in_literature: Known (the amplification formula is precisely why rank comparisons reduce to corner sizes).
salvage: Wick first-letter stripping and prefix structure foreshadow the Fox-cocycle prefix sums (d1.2.1); analyst inference.

description: Ultralimit of bulk-matching automorphisms: module maps properly into itself
obstruction: Matching bulk embeddings by automorphisms and passing to an ultralimit should give a module mapping properly into itself, but the operator-norm control needed for a contradiction is missing.
lesson: Ultralimit self-inclusion needs operator-norm control that is unavailable.
known_in_literature: apparently new (unverifiable)

description: Fock-space extra sectors; wreath-product superrigidity; norm-ideal invariants
obstruction: Fock-space constructions give extra representation sectors, but the inverse transformation need not preserve the selected subspace. BDIP would need the isomorphism to preserve enlarged components. The Ioana-Popa-Vaes superrigidity of generalized wreath products needs specific group bases, not arbitrary free bases. Voiculescu's norm-ideal (quasicentral modulus) invariants are destroyed by rough ge…
lesson: An abstract isomorphism need not preserve ANY auxiliary structure used to build an invariant (C14).
generality: general: rules out every presentation-dependent invariant
known_in_literature: Known: this is why generator-independence is the crux (Voiculescu's invariance problem for delta; Connes-Shlyakhtenko).
influence: DECISIVE: it is reapplied at a17.3, a22 (verbatim), a29, and it is the stated content of the shift to constructive changes of generators (L197-199, L201-202).

description: Replicate a hypothetical isomorphism to amplify the free-entropy-dimension gap
obstruction: Replicating a hypothetical isomorphism preserves its free-entropy-dimension ratio; iteration raises reconstruction complexity together with the gap. Continuity moduli are uncontrolled and Fock-space compactness is not preserved. Coordinatewise quantization blocks the step from large microstate packing numbers to a topological obstruction.
lesson: Amplifying a dimension gap by iteration fails because the maps are not uniformly continuous.
known_in_literature: apparently new formulation; uses known tools
salvage: The idea of iterating a generator-changing map returns at a24 and, inverted, in the final iteration (d1.2.2).

description: Fox derivatives as an obstruction (closability, filtering)
obstruction: Fox derivatives cannot be made into an invariant: closability is unavailable (a17.1), filtering leaves an (n-1)-dimensional cycle space (a17.2), the domain does not contain images of an arbitrary isomorphism (a17.3), and relative homology gives nothing (a17.4).
lesson: Fox derivatives fail as an OBSTRUCTION, but their prefix-suffix calculus is a usable tool (C15).
known_in_literature: Fox calculus is classical (Fox, Annals 1953, cited by the paper but not the trace); its closability issues are known (Thom; Alekseev-Kyed)
influence: contributory to the core lemma (tool, not idea)
salvage: Cocycle rule D_gb = D_g + lambda(g) D_b and prefix sums: paper eq:flow-cocycle, Lemma lem:cocycle-prefixes (d1.2.1, L272-279)

description: Closability via Thom / Alekseev-Kyed / Popa-Vaes
obstruction: Fox derivatives on L(F_n) with affiliated values: closability would need Thom's affiliated L2-cohomology, Alekseev-Kyed measure-continuity or Popa-Vaes, and none gives the required closability.
lesson: No closability statement is available for the Fox derivations.
known_in_literature: Known (closability of free difference quotients is understood for semicircular generators, not after arbitrary changes of generators).
salvage: Fox derivatives retained as a tool (C15)

description: Filter prefix-suffix coefficients onto a diagonal subgroup
obstruction: Filtering derivative limits onto a diagonal subgroup leaves a cycle space of dimension n-1, so no vanishing relation strong enough to compare generator counts appears.
lesson: Filtering leaves an (n-1)-dimensional residue (cf. b1^(2)(F_n) = n-1), so there is no rank contradiction.
known_in_literature: Consistent with known l2-Betti number b1^(2)(F_n) = n-1
salvage: The prefix-suffix structure of Fox derivatives (C15) is salvaged and becomes the cocycle rule D_gb = D_g + lambda(g) D_b (paper eq:flow-cocycle).

description: Domain obstacle: images of an arbitrary isomorphism need not lie in the domain
obstruction: Even a closable derivation would not settle the problem, because an arbitrary isomorphism's images need not lie in the domain.
lesson: Closability is insufficient because of the domain obstacle (C10, C14).
known_in_literature: Known (standard).

description: Relative L2-homology over a hyperfinite subfactor (Bermudez)
obstruction: Bermudez's relative L2-homology over a hyperfinite subfactor gives no distinction the model can establish.
lesson: Relative L2-homology is not computable or invariant here.
known_in_literature: Known open status

description: Conditional corner absorption under an affirmative hypothesis (seek contradiction)
obstruction: Assuming the affirmative answer gives computable corner formulas (pM0p = pP0p * L(F2)), but no contradiction: absorption maps lack compactness or surjectivity, entropy bounds and property (T) do not control free products, and complementedness is blocked.
lesson: Consequences of an affirmative answer are self-consistent as far as the model can see. This is weak evidence FOR the affirmative, though the model does not read it that way.
known_in_literature: apparently new computations built on known formulas (Dykema-Radulescu; Avitzour)
salvage: absorption through near-identity maps (a18.2) -> final absorption scheme (inferred)

description: Modify corners of Q1*Q2; Avitzour factoriality; pM0p = pP0p * L(F2)
Absorb L(F_inf) through near-identity maps fixing P0; property (T)
obstruction: Under the affirmative hypothesis, the plan was to absorb L(F_inf) through maps fixing P0 that approximate the identity uniformly on each component's unit ball. Preimages have no compactness and the limit map is not known to be surjective. Property (T) aligns components without controlling their free product. Dykema-Radulescu compression/absorption informs the construction.
lesson: Approximate-identity absorption lacks compactness and surjectivity; property (T) controls components, not their free product.
lesson_form: negative result + salvaged idea (absorption through near-identity maps)
known_in_literature: apparently new formulation
salvage: The pattern "absorb an extra free piece through near-identity maps and pass to a limit" is exactly the shape of the final route (d1, d1.3.4-5), there applied constructively and with exact automorphis…

description: Jung / Jung-Shlyakhtenko bounds for free-product generators
obstruction: Jung strong 1-boundedness and the Jung-Shlyakhtenko property-(T) bound (delta_0 <= 1 for property-T generators) do not control arbitrary free-product generators.
lesson: Entropy bounds do not control free-product generators.
known_in_literature: Known

description: Christensen-Wang complemented-subspace route
obstruction: The Christensen-Wang complemented-subspace route is rejected because the required complementedness is obstructed by an expected copy of L(F_inf).
lesson: Complementedness is obstructed.
known_in_literature: Known in spirit (Christensen-Wang 2013)

description: Reformulate via interpolation: N2=N3 iff 1/sqrt2 in F(N2); asymptotic freeness in conditional construction
obstruction: The interpolation formulas give N_r^t = N_{1+(r-1)/t^2} and N_r*N_s = N_{r+s}. With t = 1/sqrt2, N_2^{1/sqrt2} = N_3, so N2 = N3 iff 1/sqrt2 lies in F(N2). This is a correct reformulation, equivalent to the problem. The asymptotic-freeness investigation of the conditional construction gave no result.
lesson: The problem is equivalent to fundamental-group membership; the reformulation does not decide it (C16).
lesson_form: reformulation of the problem + salvaged tool (amplification calculus)
known_in_literature: Known (Dykema 1994; Radulescu 1994; standard).
influence: DECISIVE for the last step of the final proof
salvage: The amplification calculus is carried forward and used for the final step: the rank-3/4 isomorphism is transferred to ranks 2/3 (L288-289, L336-339; paper sec "Amplification to rank two").

description: Long alternating words vs component ultrapowers; nonseparable intertwining; deformation embeddings
obstruction: Long alternating words with nonperiodic letters conjugate W*(a,b^2) freely away from the component ultrapowers, which defeats the intended embedding obstruction. The cancellation bound depended on syllable length rather than on the letters, with the outer letter orthogonal to the smaller algebra.
lesson: Free products let you conjugate subalgebras away from ultrapowers, so this embedding obstruction is void.
known_in_literature: Related to known asymptotic-orthogonality phenomena in free products (Popa 1983; Popa 2014 on independence in ultraproducts)
salvage: "Long alternating words" foreshadow the long prefix words of d1.2.1 (inference)

description: Free shift vs its square (entropy); Gibbs transport; hiding directions on small supports
obstruction: A free shift conjugated to its square shows no entropy distinction (Brown-Dykema-Shlyakhtenko); Gibbs/free monotone transport preserves the number of variables; supported semicirculars suggest hiding directions on small supports.
lesson: Transport and entropy of shifts cannot change or detect the number of variables.
known_in_literature: Known (Guionnet-Shlyakhtenko 2014 give isomorphisms W*(X_1..X_n) = L(F_n) with the same n)
salvage: "hiding directions on small supports" foreshadows absorption (inference)

description: Commuting Haar witnesses -> free triple b, c1 b c1*, c2 b c2*; partition dimensions 3d vs 1+d
obstruction: Commuting Haar witnesses c1, c2, free from b, give the free triple b, c1 b c1*, c2 b c2*. Free dimension compares partition dimensions 3d and 1+d with d = 1 - sum t_j^2 and 1/2 < d < 2/3, which suggests room in rank two. But an abstract isomorphism need not preserve the partition algebra or the witnesses, and the embeddings are nonstandard.
lesson: Free-dimension counts depend on the embedding; an isomorphism need not preserve witnesses (C14).
known_in_literature: Known (Dykema 1993: standard vs nonstandard embeddings).
salvage: The device of free conjugates of a fixed variable by Haar unitaries (b, c b c*) reappears as S_g = A_g S A_g^* in the final flow (L262-271; paper Lemma lem:conjugates). This is analyst inference; the…

description: Sweep of earlier routes (survey, interpolation, absorption, rescaling, Jacobians, cohomology, s1b, cost, trace scaling, Shen, Fock rows, Hilbert transforms)
obstruction: A sweep of previously tried routes (survey, interpolation, absorption, rescaling, Jacobians, cohomology, s1b, cost, trace scaling, Shen, Fock rows, Hilbert transforms). Each is blocked by an earlier clause.
lesson: All known invariants are blocked; the open requirement is control of arbitrary generator changes without quantitative regularity.
known_in_literature: n/a
influence: contributory: prepares the shift of focus to generator changes (L197-199, L201-202)

description: Iterate a hypothetical n->m semicircular transformation; free subgroup words; orbital entropy
obstruction: Iterating a hypothetical transformation from n semicircular generators to m>n would give m^k outputs from n^k inputs. But the errors satisfy e_j <= delta_j + L_j e_{j-1} with uncontrolled Lipschitz constants L_j (f is only measurable), and fixing the final accuracy forces increasingly precise earlier layers. Free subgroup words restore polynomial control but lose microstate extendability; orbital…
lesson: Error compounding through rough maps blocks iterative amplification (C17).
lesson_form: negative result + salvaged structure (iteration with error budgets)
generality: general (any iterative scheme with measurable maps)
known_in_literature: The error recursion is standard; its failure is a generic barrier, not a known named result.
influence: decisive-to-contributory (analyst inference: the summary does not draw the link)
salvage: INVERTED in the final route: choose each future budget AFTER the current approximating word is fixed (L286-288, L316; paper eq:future-budget, fig:iteration). The final iteration also changes the size…

description: Tail permutations; Baire; Sobolev closability; graph products; max-amenable; free Stein dimension
obstruction: Tail permutations are outer and give no implementing unitaries for central sequences; the Baire argument loses a uniform interior radius; even with Sobolev regularity, closability of delta does not give closability of P delta. Graph-product rigidity and maximal-amenable uniqueness (Hayes-Jekel-Kunnawalkam Elayavalli) give no rank calculation; free Stein dimension (Charlesworth-Nelson) is algebrai…
lesson: Baire loses a uniform radius (C18); the remaining invariants are uncomputable here.
known_in_literature: Known (each tool's limitations are documented in the cited works)
influence: contributory (C18 reused at b1.4, "no Baire smoothing")

description: Finite Fourier-support images; subgroup surjectivity / abelianization
obstruction: Restricting to finite Fourier-support images of the canonical unitaries; subgroup surjectivity/abelianization hoped to detect rank. This is left open, with no stated failure.
lesson: No lesson is stated; the target is sharpened to "control of arbitrary generator changes without quantitative regularity".
known_in_literature: n/a
influence: contributory to the reorientation at L201-202

description: Matrix entries and free compression rank obstruction
obstruction: Wick words follow paths through matrix indices, and free compression interpolates between a change of generators and its covariance. Rare contractions can preserve invertibility despite unfavourable dimension counts, and iterative encodings force increasingly rough decoders.
lesson: Dimension counting cannot obstruct changes of generators (C17 again).
known_in_literature: apparently new formulation

description: Automatic continuity / Peterson-Thom consequences as control on rough generator changes
obstruction: Ringrose, Alekseev-Kyed and Popa-Vaes continuity hypotheses do not extend to arbitrary affiliated-valued derivations; Peterson-Thom consequences give no rank invariant.
lesson: No automatic-continuity control of rough generator changes (C7 again).
known_in_literature: Known

description: BDIP sans-rank + Dykema-Zhao rescaling; Nielsen substitutions; absorption + IPP
obstruction: BDIP sans-rank + Dykema-Zhao: changing the separable parameter leaves the nonseparable component count unchanged. Nielsen substitutions mix components and destroy the commutation relations needed to transfer a separable isomorphism to the enlargements. Under Dykema-Radulescu absorption, separate IPP conjugacies do not control the free complement.
lesson: Nonseparable enlargements and rigidity are useless once generator changes (Nielsen) are allowed (C1, C2, C14).
known_in_literature: Known
influence: decisive as the last straw before the restart (L221)
salvage: Nielsen substitutions as a tool: reappear constructively as the inverse Nielsen automorphism (L314-315; paper Prop. prop:perturbation, C' = C A_w^*). This is analyst inference.

description: Strategy POS: construct a change of generators (recover a missing generator)
obstruction: Recovering a generator is possible once freeness is broken, but exact freeness and generation cannot both hold in a finite perturbation (C19a, C19).
lesson: Constructive recovery must preserve exact freeness at each stage; generation must come from a limit.
known_in_literature: apparently new framing

description: Ornstein-Weiss analogy: free Haar vertex variables on the Cayley tree; free edge increments; missing root
obstruction: The Cayley-tree construction recovers generation but loses freeness; transport cannot repair the correlations; spectral gap forbids nearby free generating tuples.
lesson: Constructive recovery is possible in principle, but exact freeness must be preserved and generation must be a limit phenomenon (C19a, C19).
known_in_literature: Classical analogue known (Ornstein-Weiss 1987; Bowen 2010); free version apparently new

description: Nonzero-mean vertex unitaries recover the root (telescoping) - "Aha!"
obstruction: Free Haar vertex variables x_g on the Cayley tree have free edge increments x_g* x_{g s_i}, but reconstruction needs the missing root x_e. A classical analogy (Ornstein-Weiss) says that with non-uniform labels the shift ambiguity is resolved by empirical frequencies. With nonzero mean beta, telescoping and weak convergence give x_g* x_h -> beta x_g*, recovering every vertex, but neighbouring edge…
lesson: A missing generator can be recovered if freeness is sacrificed; the whole difficulty is keeping exact freeness (C19a).
generality: general (identifies the true constraint: exact freeness + generation)
known_in_literature: Classical analogue known: the Ornstein-Weiss factor map from the 2-shift onto the 4-shift over F_2 uses edge differences; Bowen (Annals 2010) shows these Bernoulli shifts are nonisomorphic. The free-…
salvage: The "absorb/recover a missing generator from words in the others" framing is carried into POS2 (L260-261; paper Prop. prop:perturbation).

description: Free monotone transport to remove correlations
obstruction: Free monotone transport was considered to remove the correlations, but the required regularity was not established.
lesson: Transport needs analytic regularity that the correlated tuple lacks.
known_in_literature: Known limitation (Guionnet-Shlyakhtenko require small analytic perturbations of semicircular laws)

description: Norm convergence of averages of conjugate site variables
Spectral gap: no free generating tuple near the free tuple (d>=2)
obstruction: For d >= 2 a spectral gap bars nearby free generating tuples: the root would become an impossible approximate intertwiner. A nonfree generating set accumulates at a free tuple that is separated from all free generating tuples, so there is no Baire smoothing.
lesson: Free generating tuples cannot be reached by small perturbation of this nonfree generating construction, so generation must be obtained in a limit, not at a finite stage (C19).
lesson_form: negative result + constraint on future approaches
known_in_literature: apparently new as stated (it uses spectral gap / non-amenability, which is known)
influence: contributory (the final route keeps exact freeness at every stage and gets generation only in the limit, L286-288 and L316-319); inferred, low confidence

description: Strategy NEG (again): generator-independent microstate invariant
obstruction: Re-entry into microstate invariants repeats C7, C8, C1, C11 and C4 ("Same old").
lesson: NEG is exhausted.
known_in_literature: Known

description: Microstate invariant via polynomial approximation
obstruction: Microstate invariant: the polynomial approximation P(V) is close to U, but the derivative of the difference can be huge, so there is no closability.
lesson: Same as C8/C7.
known_in_literature: Known

description: Jung hyperfinite inequality; zero-entropy shifts; separable MASAs; Shen/DSSW; commutator invariant
obstruction: Jung's hyperfinite inequality does not carry finite-Borel-operation estimates through strong limits; zero-entropy free shifts (Stormer); separable MASAs lose BDIP's cardinal distinction; Shen/DSSW estimates still lack a positive lower bound; the commutator invariant confronts algebraic vs von Neumann generation.
lesson: Strong limits destroy finite-operation estimates; the other invariants are blocked by C1, C10 and C11.
known_in_literature: Known

description: Urysohn width + Borsuk-Ulam spectral clipping
obstruction: Urysohn width suggests obstructing an encoding of free tuples through fewer matrix generators. Spectral clipping and Borsuk-Ulam control the whole operator-norm ball, but the obstruction cannot be restricted uniformly to a prescribed free law, and projection onto one coordinate defeats the global-negation argument.
lesson: Global topological width bounds do not localise to a free law (C20a).
known_in_literature: Analogous to known gaps between waist/width inequalities and measure concentration

description: Packing rank, s1b, transport, ultrapower-embedding mixtures
obstruction: Packing rank (Jung's rank theorem) and strong 1-boundedness do not distinguish the factors; transport has regularity restrictions; mixtures of ultrapower embeddings (Brown) give insufficient matrix-dimension growth.
lesson: The remaining entropy-type invariants are constant or insufficient (C4 again).
known_in_literature: Known
influence: decisive as the last straw before the final restart (L260)

description: Strategy POS (final): absorb a free generator by small automorphisms and a limit
Absorb a free generator through small perturbations
Straight cocycle paths
obstruction: Straight (linear) cocycle paths produce nearly translation-invariant elements, which obstructs approximating a free complement. On a nonamenable group, near-invariance forces smallness.
lesson: Linear interpolation of perturbations fails; a genuinely nonlinear, trace-preserving flow is needed (C20).
known_in_literature: Uses the known spectral gap / non-amenability of F_n
influence: DECISIVE (immediate replacement by the polynomial flow, L261-266)
salvage: The word "cocycle" survives: the cocycle D on F_n becomes the coefficient object of the flow (L272; paper eq:flow-cocycle).

description: Polynomial flow driven by conjugates U_g S U_g^* of a complementary semicircular S
obstruction: The first flow used a complementary SEMICIRCULAR S. That forced a measurable Haar reparametrization of S to reach the Haar generator C, and raised the open question of whether a continuous Haar function could generate the semicircular algebra while approximating the oscillatory exponential. It also relied on semicircular stability to keep residuals small. None of these failed outright; the whole …
lesson: Drive the flow by a function of the generator to be absorbed (S = Arg C, e^{iS} = C), not by an independent semicircular variable.
lesson_form: salvaged tool (flow, small cocycle, iteration) + superseded representation
known_in_literature: Cyclomorphy (Voiculescu 2002) is the known framework for exponentiating trace-preserving polynomial vector fields on semicircular-type generators
salvage: Everything except the choice of S is kept: the flow (paper Prop. prop:flow), the small cocycle (Lemma lem:small-cocycle), the iteration and the amplification transfer.

description: Fox derivatives of long words + prefix-sum cutoff inverse (small cocycle)
Measurable Haar reparametrization of S, free-basis change, diagonal iteration with budgets, amplification transfer

obstruction: Checking operator-norm approximation against reduced group C*-algebra invariants separates measurable coordinate changes from continuous calculus.
